transcript.text:
If your hob isn’t working properly, first make it safe:

• Gas smell: Turn off the gas supply if safe, open windows, don’t use electrical switches or flames, and contact your gas emergency service/qualified engineer.
• Sparking, burning smell, cracked glass, or tripping electrics: Switch it off at the isolator/fuse box and arrange repair.

A few common checks, depending on the type:

### Electric / ceramic hob
• Check the circuit breaker or cooker switch hasn’t tripped.
• Make sure the control lock/child lock isn’t enabled.
• Let it cool fully, then clean and dry the controls—moisture can cause touch controls to misbehave.
• If one ring does not heat but others do, its element or control may have failed.

### Induction hob
• Ensure you are using a magnetic, induction-compatible pan; a magnet should stick to its base.
• Put the pan centrally on the zone and make sure the base is flat and not too small.
• Check for error codes on the display and consult the model manual.
• Power-cycle it: switch off at the wall/isolator for a few minutes, then restore power.

### Gas hob
• Confirm the gas supply is on and other gas appliances work.
• Clean and dry the burner cap, crown, and ignition electrode; food spills and moisture often stop ignition.
• Ensure burner parts are seated correctly and the small flame ports are not blocked.
• If it clicks continuously, dry the area and leave it switched off for a while; moisture around the igniter is common.
• A weak/yellow flame, gas smell, or burners that won’t stay lit needs a qualified gas engineer.

Tell me:
1. Is it gas, electric ceramic, or induction?
2. What exactly happens—won’t turn on, no heat, error code, keeps clicking, trips power, uneven flame?
3. Is it affecting every burner/zone or only one?
It's an electric ceramic hob, a Zanussi. Only the rear right ring isn't heating, the other three are fine. The display still shows the power level for it though.

Because the other three zones work and the rear-right zone still accepts/displays a power level, the hob’s mains supply and main controls are likely fine. The fault is usually local to that zone, such as:

• failed heating element/radiant ring
• loose or burnt wiring/connector to that element
• failed zone relay or power-control module
• less commonly, a temperature limiter/sensor fault

Safe checks you can do:

1. Switch the hob off at its isolator/circuit breaker and let it cool completely.
2. Check whether the zone has any residual-heat indication after being set to a high level for a few minutes.
• If it never becomes warm and no residual-heat symbol appears, the element/control circuit is likely open or not being powered.
3. Turn power off for 5–10 minutes, then restore it and retest. This can clear an occasional control fault, though it is unlikely if the fault persists.
4. If it is a touch-control model, make sure the surface is dry and there is no pan or object covering the controls—but since it shows the selected setting, this is unlikely to be the cause.

Do not remove the glass top or access internal wiring unless you are competent to work on isolated mains appliances. Ceramic hobs contain high-voltage components and can retain hazardous energy.

A repair engineer should be able to test the rear-right element’s resistance and whether voltage is reaching it. If the element has failed, it can often be replaced; whether it is economical depends on the hob’s age, model, and the cost of the specific dual/standard radiant element.

If you provide the full Zanussi model/PNC number from the rating label (often on the underside, in the manual, or installation paperwork), I can help identify whether that rear-right zone is a standard or dual element and what part/fault is most likely.
I haven't got the full model number, only that the manual cover says it starts ZHRN. It's about 8 years old. Does that help?

Yes—ZHRN identifies the Zanussi hob range, but not the exact variant or spare part. There are several very similar models (for example, different widths, control layouts, and single/dual-zone elements), so the full model or PNC number is still needed before ordering anything.

For an approximately 8-year-old Zanussi ceramic hob with one completely cold zone but a normal power-level display, the most likely fault remains:

1. Failed rear-right radiant heating element — most common.
2. Burnt/loose connection to that element.
3. Faulty power regulator/relay on the control board — less common, but possible.

It is generally repairable, and if it is only the element or wiring, repair can still be worthwhile at that age. A control-board fault may be more expensive.

To find the exact details, look for a rating label with something like:

• Model: ZHRN…
• PNC / Prod. No.: usually a 9-digit number beginning 911…
• Serial number

It is normally on the underside of the hob, so it may require looking in the cupboard below it or, if inaccessible, having the hob lifted out by a competent installer/engineer. It may also be on the original invoice, installation paperwork, or inside the manual’s back pages.

Until repaired, avoid using that rear-right zone. The other zones can normally still be used if there are no burning smells, electrical buzzing, cracking glass, or tripping breakers.
I can't see a label without taking the hob out, and I'm not doing that. There was a slight burnt smell from that ring once a couple of weeks ago, but not since. Should I get an engineer in?
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
Sorry, I think your last message didn't come through. Should I get an engineer in for the rear right ring?

Yes—given the ring has stopped heating and you noticed a burnt smell, it would be sensible to get a qualified appliance repair engineer to inspect it.

A burnt smell can indicate an overheated or loose terminal, damaged wiring, a failed element, or a failed control component. Even if the smell has not returned, avoid using that rear-right zone and ideally switch the hob off at its isolator when it is unattended.

You can usually continue using the other three zones only if:

• there is no current burning smell, smoke, crackling/buzzing, or visible damage;
• the hob is not tripping the circuit breaker/RCD;
• the glass is not cracked; and
• the rear-right zone remains switched off.

If any smell returns, the controls behave oddly, the hob trips power, or you see damage, turn the whole hob off at the cooker isolator and stop using it until checked.

When booking, say: “Zanussi ceramic electric hob, around 8 years old; rear-right zone displays power level but does not heat; there was a previous slight burning smell.” The engineer can obtain the rating details after safely isolating/lifting the hob if required.
